function_question: How does nature find the way home?

opening.text: There was a boy called Kian whose family had just moved to a new town.
Kian walked into his big new school, where long corridors and lots of doors all looked the same.
The bell rang for music, and Kian took a wrong turn, then another. He arrived late, again. "There has to be an easier way to find things here," he thought.

card.goal: A way-finding system any new kid can follow
card.rules: Test it with someone who's never done the route

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Kian is new at a big school, and he keeps getting lost. Can you help him design a way-finding system any new kid can follow? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some designers already have a spark of an idea for helping people find their way. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Animals have been finding their way home for millions of years. Tap each card to meet four super navigators!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which kind of clue will lead your helper along the route with the fewest wrong turns?
guide.sketch: Time to draw a map of your route and mark every tricky turn, like a real designer!
guide.build_and_test: Put up your system and ask someone new to follow it. How many wrong turns do they make?
guide.retry_tip: Designers never stop at round 1. Add ONE better clue at the trickiest turn, and test again with someone new!
guide.ending: And ever since then, every new kid at Kian's school follows YOUR clues on their first day, and nobody arrives lost and late.

quick_check.question: From the front door, Kian walks 30 steps to the stairs, then 20 steps to the music room. How many steps is that altogether?
quick_check.right: Right! 30 + 20 = 50 steps. A desert ant keeps count like this all the way from its nest.
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Add the two parts of the walk together.

clue_cards.name: Desert ant
clue_cards.trick: It counts its steps and uses the sun as a compass.
clue_cards.does: It walks straight home across flat sand with no landmarks.

clue_cards.name: Honeybee
clue_cards.trick: It remembers trees, ponds and flower beds along the way.
clue_cards.does: It flies back to its hive and to its favourite flowers.

clue_cards.name: Sea turtle
clue_cards.does: It swims thousands of kilometres back to the beach where it hatched.

clue_cards.name: Salmon
clue_cards.trick: It remembers the smell of its home stream.
clue_cards.does: It follows that smell upstream after years at sea.

predict.prompt: Landmark clue or counting clue? Predict first!

items.label: Turn left at the big red door

predict.explain: Landmarks are things you can see or hear along the way. Counting clues use numbers, like steps or doors. Using both together is much safer than just one.

lab.title: The route lab
lab.predict: You guide a helper along a route with 3 turns. Which clue will cause the fewest wrong turns?

tool.name: Nature Translator
tool.intro: You already know F (Function) and Q (Nature question). Today you'll learn the last 2 steps, S and D, and translate all the way from nature back to your design.

parts.name: Strategy
parts.what: Name a living thing that does the job, and say HOW it does it.
parts.example: ☂️ A lotus leaf is covered in tiny waxy bumps, so rain rolls right off.
parts.starter: The desert ant finds home by…

parts.name: Design principle
parts.what: Say the trick in plain words, without the animal or plant.
parts.example: ☂️ A bumpy, waxy surface makes water roll away.
parts.starter: A way-finding system could use… so that…

sketch_checklist: I drew a map of the whole route.
I marked every decision point where someone could go wrong.
I showed at least 2 kinds of clues at the trickiest turn.

test.check_question: Tester check: how sure did your tester feel?
check_options: Unsure at one or two spots

reflection.question: Which nature trick helped your system most?
